 We build the platform that gets Okta's code tested, merged, built, and shipped. Bacon, our CI system, runs tens of thousands of tests on every commit. Around it we own the services that make CI observable and self-healing, and the release tooling that takes a green commit to a production release: code freeze, backporting, release assembly, artifact promotion, and release auditing. 
 We are a small team, we ship weekly, and engineers own services end to end. Our goals are to cut feedback time from hours to minutes, keep mainline green, and make every release predictable, auditable, and boring. 
 Our engineering team is fast, innovative and flexible; with a weekly release cycle and individual ownership. We expect great things from our engineers and reward them with stimulating new projects, emerging technologies and the chance to be part of a company that is changing the cloud computing landscape forever.

 Release engineering 
 Own and evolve the release toolchain: code freeze, backporting to release branches, release assembly, artifact promotion, and release auditing. You'll build the automation and Slack workflows (for example in Baconbot) that engineers rely on. 
 Keep weekly releases on schedule. That includes release branch health, cherry-pick/backport gaps, and promotion of build artifacts through environments. 
 Build controls and audit trails that prove what shipped, from where, and who approved it, supporting compliance requirements without slowing teams down. 
 Run the release process during freezes and incidents. You'll triage blocked releases, retry or unstick commits, and write the post-incident follow-ups. 
 CI platform 
 Design, build, and operate the services behind Bacon: REST/GraphQL APIs, data pipelines, and the React frontend, in Java, Python, Node/TypeScript, and Go. 
 Improve CI speed, reliability, and cost across runner infrastructure on AWS, host images, queue and job allocation, and flaky-test detection and quarantine. 
 Make CI and releases observable with telemetry, metrics, and dashboards (OpenTelemetry, Grafana, time-series stores) that show why a build or release failed and how healthy the fleet is. 
 Apply LLMs to developer workflows, such as automated log triage and failure root-causing, with sensible guardrails. 
 Across both 
 Automate everything. Everybody automates here, so you'll write tools and scripts that remove toil for thousands of internal users. 
 Partner with product engineering, QA, and Ops teams on rollouts, adoption, and feedback. 
 Share operational ownership: on-call participation, runbooks, alerting, and incident follow-up for what you build.

 3+ years of professional software development in one or more of Python, Java, Go, or JavaScript/TypeScript 
 Experience building and running CI/CD and release pipelines, including branching strategies, versioning, and artifact management 
 Strong Git skills: release branches, cherry-picking/backporting, merge conflict resolution, and release tagging 
 Experience building and running backend services and APIs (microservices, multi-service systems) 
 Hands-on experience with AWS (for example Lambda, SQS, EC2, S3) or Kubernetes 
 Working knowledge of Linux, Docker, and shell scripting

 Ability to coordinate cross-functional work to completion and communicate clearly with internal customers, including during time-sensitive releases

 Infrastructure as code (Terraform, Packer) and host or AMI image builds

WHO ARE WE?

Key Overview:
As a Member of Technical Staff in Post-Training, you will train our large language models (LLMs) with reinforcement learning and develop methods that help them generalize beyond the distribution they were trained on. You will design the training recipes, environments, and evaluations that tell us whether a model has truly learned a skill or has only fitted its training tasks, and turn what works into the recipes behind our production models. You will work closely with the post-training data infrastructure, evaluation, and pre-training teams.

Key Responsibilities

 - Design, run, and analyse large-scale RL post-training experiments (e.g., RLHF, RL from verifiable rewards).

 - Research and develop methods that improve out-of-distribution generalization, such as reward design, environment and task diversity, curricula, and regularization.

 - Build held-out evaluations that measure generalization to unseen tasks, domains, and formats, and that catch reward hacking and benchmark overfitting.

 - Diagnose training dynamics and failure modes, including instability, reward over-optimization, and capability regressions.

 - Turn successful research into robust, reproducible training recipes for production models.

Qualifications

 - Strong research and software engineering skills, with hands-on experience training LLMs.

 - Experience applying reinforcement learning to LLMs (e.g., PPO, GRPO, RLHF, RLVR), ideally at scale.

 - Track record of work on generalization, robustness, or distribution shift, through publications or shipped models.

 - Rigorous experimental practice: clean ablations, careful controls, and sound conclusions from noisy results.

THE ROLE

We are looking for an AI Enablement Lead to help build and scale how our organization works with AI. This role sits within People & Culture because our opportunity with AI is fundamentally about people, capability, and how work gets done. The AI Enablement Lead will be responsible for building the skills, habits, systems, and community that enable employees to use AI effectively, responsibly, and consistently across the company.

This is not an AI engineering role. Instead, this person will operate at the intersection of AI, learning, organizational change, and business transformation. A core part of the role will be building and leading our AI Superteam: a cross-functional network of AI experts and champions embedded within each department. These individuals will maintain their existing functional reporting lines while having a dotted-line relationship to the AI Enablement Lead. Together, this network will identify opportunities, test new ways of working, share best practices, and scale high-impact AI use cases across the organization.

The ideal candidate is both AI-fluent and highly people-oriented. They do not need to be the deepest technical AI expert in the company. They need to understand what AI can enable, translate that into practical changes in how people work, and bring people together to make those changes stick.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

AI ENABLEMENT STRATEGY

 - Develop and execute a company-wide strategy for AI capability, adoption, and enablement in partnership with leadership, Technology, Security, Legal, and business teams.

 - Identify the skills, behaviours, and ways of working employees will need as AI becomes increasingly embedded in our work.

 - Build a practical roadmap for moving the organization from AI awareness to meaningful adoption and measurable impact.

AI SUPERTEAM

 - Build, coordinate, and lead a cross-functional AI Superteam made up of designated AI experts from across the organization.

 - Establish a clear operating model, expectations, priorities, and cadence for the Superteam.

 - Create a forum where teams can share experiments, successful use cases, challenges, and emerging AI practices.

 - Partner with department AI experts to identify high-value opportunities and help move promising experiments from individual use cases into scalable organizational practices.

 - Create mechanisms for knowledge-sharing so that an AI innovation in one function can be discovered and adapted by others.

LEARNING & CAPABILITY BUILDING

 - Design and deliver role-based AI learning experiences for employees, managers, and leaders.

 - Build practical resources such as playbooks, use-case libraries, prompt frameworks, guides, workshops, and office hours.

 - Help employees develop the judgment required to evaluate AI-generated work for accuracy, quality, usefulness, completeness, and appropriate human review.

 - Develop AI learning pathways that evolve as tools and organizational needs change.

ADOPTION & CHANGE MANAGEMENT

 - Drive adoption of AI tools and new AI-enabled ways of working across the organization.

 - Partner with leaders and teams to identify where AI can meaningfully improve productivity, quality, decision-making, or employee experience.

 - Help teams move beyond experimentation toward sustainable changes in workflows and operating practices.

 - Identify and address barriers to adoption, including capability gaps, confidence, behaviour, process friction, and unclear expectations.

MEASUREMENT & CONTINUOUS IMPROVEMENT

 - Assess where employees and teams are making effective use of AI and where additional enablement is required.

 - Gather feedback and insights from the AI Superteam and broader employee population to continuously improve our AI strategy and programs.

 - Share progress, learnings, and recommendations with senior leadership.

WHAT THIS ROLE DOES, AND DOES NOT, OWN

The AI Enablement Lead owns organizational AI capability and adoption.

This includes:

 - AI learning and enablement

 - AI adoption and change management

 - AI community and the AI Superteam

 - Cross-functional knowledge sharing

 - Role-based AI capability development

 - Measurement of AI readiness, adoption, and impact

 - Identification and scaling of proven AI practices

This role does not independently own:

 - AI product or software engineering

 - Enterprise AI architecture

 - Cybersecurity or data security controls

 - Legal or privacy policy

 - Technical procurement or infrastructure

The AI Enablement Lead will partner closely with the teams responsible for these areas to ensure that employee enablement and technical governance evolve together.

HOW THE AI SUPERTEAM WORKS

Each major function will designate an AI Expert / AI Champion who remains embedded within their department while maintaining a dotted-line relationship to the AI Enablement Lead.

These departmental AI experts will:

 - Identify AI opportunities within their function

 - Experiment with new tools and workflows

 - Help colleagues adopt effective AI practices

 - Bring functional challenges and learnings to the Superteam

 - Share successful use cases across the organization

 - Partner on cross-functional AI initiatives

 - Help identify emerging skills and capability needs within their function

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

In the first 12–24 months, success could include:

 - A functioning AI Superteam with strong participation across key functions

 - Clear AI capability expectations and learning pathways for employees

 - Meaningful growth in employee confidence and effective AI usage

 - A growing library of validated, high-impact AI use cases

 - AI practices successfully scaling across multiple departments

 - Managers increasingly incorporating AI into how work is designed and delegated

 - Evidence that AI is improving productivity, quality, speed, or employee experience

 - A clear understanding of the skills and capabilities our workforce will need as AI continues to evolve

THE PROFILE WE ARE LOOKING FOR

 - You are comfortable experimenting with new technology, but you are equally interested in the organizational challenge of helping hundreds of people adopt it effectively.

 - You are a connector: you naturally bring together people, ideas, and teams.

 - You don't need to have all the answers yourself. You know how to find the people who do, create the right environment for experimentation, identify what works, and turn individual innovation into organizational capability.

 - Experience building communities of practice, champion networks, or similar grassroots enablement models is highly valued

 - Strong practical understanding of generative AI and modern AI tools

 - Hands-on experience using AI to improve real-world knowledge work

 - Ability to distinguish between interesting AI experimentation and genuinely valuable business applications

 - Strong understanding of responsible AI use, including human oversight, data considerations, quality, and appropriate judgment

 - Curiosity and comfort operating in a rapidly changing technology landscape

 - Exceptional facilitator and communicator

 - Strong change-management instincts and a bias toward experimentation and learning

SECURITY REQUIREMENTS

 - Candidates must undergo a criminal records check upon hire;

 - Be a Canadian Citizen (dual citizens included), or eligible to work in Canada;

OUR VALUES

We do things the Solink way:

OUR COMPANY COMPETENCIES

 - Customer Focus - We are putting customer impact at the center of our decisions, using insights, data, and feedback to deliver consistent value today while shaping long-term trust, loyalty, and sustainable growth.

 - Systems Thinking - We are designing and evolving processes, tools, and operating models so reliable outcomes can occur without individual intervention.

 - AI Amplified Execution - We are thoughtfully integrating AI into how work gets done, not just to move faster, but to solve better problems, redesign workflows, and create scalable advantage.

 - Outcome Ownership - We take full accountability for the results we create, including the decisions, compromises, successes, and failures, and using those outcomes to improve future performance.

Builders have downloaded it more than 500 million times.
 Laravel Cloud is our commercial platform: a cloud built around the frameworks teams already use, for new and existing applications alike. It runs Laravel, Symfony, Next.js, Nuxt, Django, FastAPI, Ruby on Rails, Go, Rust, and more. It's a fully managed platform with compute, databases, caches, queues, and scale-to-zero, so teams can spend their time on the product instead of the infrastructure. You'll work with engineering teams across many languages and frameworks, from a single builder running a substantial product to established companies serving hundreds of millions of requests a week.

Our Solutions Engineers have a repeatable approach to discovery, enterprise trials, and migrations. With a strong product-market fit and a brand that opens doors, you'll join a small, experienced team that will help you grow into the role.
 In this role, you connect technical discovery to business value for Laravel Cloud. You partner with our Account Executives from the first discovery call through a customer's first production migration. You run enterprise trials and show prospects how their applications will run on our platform.
 Why this job is unique
 Our audience is developers . They have high standards, deep expertise, and no time for a sales pitch that lacks substance.
 Empathy earns trust . Understanding their challenges is how you build lasting relationships.
 You'll help shape what comes next . Our process is working, and we keep refining it. We want your ideas for making it even better as the team grows.
 What you'll do
 Accelerate the sales motion . You lead the technical charge to win new business. This means running discovery, mapping complex application ecosystems and hosting needs to our platform, and delivering high-fidelity solution designs and estimates.
 Partner with Account Executives . You work alongside Account Executives to guide prospects from evaluation to their first migration.
 Lead enterprise trials . You own the hands-on technical work: setting up trial environments, proving performance and fit, and getting customer teams ready for production.
 Talk architecture and first principles . You walk prospects through complex architectures and migration strategies, reasoning from first principles rather than a script, from developers up to engineering leadership.
 Build the team's knowledge . You share what you learn in the field through our internal knowledge base, internal tools, and product feedback.
 Hands-on engineering experience . You've built and deployed web applications on cloud infrastructure, ideally AWS. Laravel or PHP experience is a plus, but our customers also build with Node.js, Python, Go, Ruby, and Rust, and you're comfortable working across languages and frameworks.
 Data fluency . You've worked with a range of databases and data platforms and understand their trade-offs.
 Excited to be a part of Sales . You want to work with prospects and customers and enjoy explaining complex architectures and migration plans.
 Clear communication . You listen first and can explain technical concepts to anyone, from developers to finance.

 The opportunity
 Limitless Talent places closers, setters, client success managers, media buyers and marketing managers for the agency owners in our programs, and hires for Limitless itself. Demand is already there: more than a dozen paid searches are open right now. We need someone who can carry real recruiting work and put a system around it.
 About Limitless
 Limitless Agency helps digital marketing agency owners build businesses that scale and sell. Our core program, Limitless Black Card, combines one-on-one strategy with the founders, implementation support, weekly group coaching and a dedicated account team. We launched Limitless Talent in September 2026 so our clients could hire A-players fast, and it's become one of our fastest-growing divisions.
 Role at a glance
 Role: Recruitment Operations Manager (Limitless Talent)
 Team: Limitless Agency, Limitless Talent
 Reports to: Director of Operations
 Type: Full-time, exclusive independent contractor. Remote, U.S. Eastern business hours.
 Location: Remote, Canada
 The role
 This is a player-coach seat. Most of your week is real recruiting: screening, interviewing, headhunting and closing candidates for client and internal roles. You also own how recruiting runs: the pipeline, the process, capacity, client updates and the weekly numbers, and you lead the recruiters who work alongside you.
 No task is beneath this role. You'll post jobs, chase no-shows and update Workable yourself when that's what it takes.
 What you will do
 Hands-on recruiting (every day) 
 Run first-round screens and interviews for client and Limitless roles.
 Headhunt every week on LinkedIn Recruiter and other channels. Don't wait for inbound.
 Write and post job ads, review applicants and keep candidates moving.
 Present shortlists and one-page candidate profiles, and close candidates through to offer and start date.
 Fill Limitless's own sales, client success and recruiting roles with a weekly screening quota.
 Delivery and speed 
 Get every new search live within 48 hours of the client's hiring alignment call.
 Deliver a first qualified shortlist within 10 business days (sooner for sales roles).
 Own the search queue: set capacity per recruiter, sequence new searches and give clients honest timelines.
 Pipeline and process 
 Run Workable like a sales pipeline: every candidate in the right stage, every interview logged as held, no-show, pass or fail within 24 hours.
 Standardize 20 to 25 minute first-round screens with pass/fail scorecards.
 Write and maintain recruiting SOPs, interview guides and job description templates.
 Use AI and automation to cut admin work.
 Talent bench, team and reporting 
 Build and run our talent community, a vetted pool of strong candidates we stay in touch with so new roles fill from the bench.
 Coach the recruiters, hold them to weekly targets and help hire new ones as we grow.
 Run client hiring alignment calls and be the escalation point when a search is off track.
 Send leadership a weekly scorecard: open searches, days to shortlist, interviews held, pass-through rates and starts.
 How we'll measure you
 Search live after alignment call: 48 hours
 First qualified shortlist to client: 10 business days or less
 Interview outcomes logged in Workable: 100%, within 24 hours
 Headhunted candidates added: 25+ a week, visible in Workable
 Internal Limitless roles: weekly screening quota hit, every week
 Talent community: 300+ vetted members by day 90
 Placements starting: 5 to 10 a month across the team, 1 to 2 of them internal Limitless hires
 4+ years of hands-on recruiting, including leading or mentoring other recruiters or running delivery at a recruiting or staffing agency.
 You still love the work itself: screening, interviewing and headhunting are part of your week.
 Experience running many searches at once and hitting time-to-fill and quality targets.
 A track record hiring sales, client success and marketing roles for U.S. companies, including remote and international hires.
 Process brain: you've built pipelines, SOPs, scorecards and reporting.
 Power user of an ATS (Workable strongly preferred) and LinkedIn Recruiter. Comfortable using AI tools every day.
 Confident with clients: you can run an alignment call, push back on unrealistic asks and protect our standards.
 Fluent English, written and spoken. Available full-time during U.S. Eastern hours, with no other jobs or side clients.
 Nice to have 
 Experience in a digital marketing agency or with agency-owner clients.
 You've built or run a talent community or candidate network.
 Experience with behavioral assessments (Predictive Index or similar).
 Prove it

 Searches you ran at the same time, with time-to-shortlist and time-to-fill.
 A pipeline, scorecard or SOP you built, and what it changed.
 A live headhunting exercise: find five strong candidates for one of our open roles.
 Who thrives here 
 You're driven, organized and fast. You do the work yourself and fix the system around it. At Hadley Designs, we believe early learning should be joyful, screen-free, and filled with connection.
 Founded by Becca Hadley, a former teacher and mom who began creating hand-drawn learning tools at her kitchen table, we’ve grown into a leading early childhood education brand trusted by millions of parents, grandparents, and teachers. Our products are developmentally sound, emotionally engaging, and intentionally designed to help children ages 3–8 grow curious, confident, and resilient.
 We serve busy, intentional families who are tired of screens and want more meaningful ways to teach and connect with their kids. From educational posters to busy books, handwriting guides to emotional learning kits, every product is crafted with care and rooted in research.
 Our vision is bold: to become the most trusted children’s brand in the world, present in millions of homes, and passed down for generations, while reaching $100 million in annual revenue by 2030.
 Today, Hadley Designs is an approximately $25 million ecommerce brand selling across Amazon, Shopify, TikTok Shop, and other channels. We've built a strong foundation, an established customer base, and a talented team of specialists. Now, our next chapter is about building a repeatable, profitable growth engine that can take us from $25 million to $100 million and beyond.
 We're looking for an entrepreneurial Director of Ecommerce Growth who has helped scale ecommerce brands before and knows how to turn growth opportunities into measurable business results. Someone who can see the bigger picture, connect the dots across channels, align talented teams, and determine where to invest, what to scale, and what to stop.
 This is an opportunity to take meaningful ownership of our growth strategy, build systems that consistently generate profitable demand, and help shape the next stage of Hadley Designs.
 Role Overview 
 The Director of Ecommerce Growth is responsible for building and leading Hadley Designs' next phase of profitable growth, developing a repeatable demand generation engine that can scale our business from $25 million to $100 million and beyond.
 This is a hands-on growth leadership role that combines strategic thinking, financial accountability, and cross-functional execution. We're looking for someone who thinks like an entrepreneur, understands the economics of scaling an ecommerce brand, and knows how to turn promising opportunities into profitable, repeatable growth systems.
 We've built a talented team of specialists across Amazon, Shopify, TikTok Shop, paid media, creative, and affiliate marketing. The Director of Ecommerce Growth connects the dots between these functions, aligning priorities, coordinating execution, removing bottlenecks, and ensuring our investments translate into measurable business results.
 This person doesn't need to be the best specialist in every channel, but they must know how to lead specialists, challenge assumptions, diagnose performance, and make the entire growth engine more effective. They take ownership of growth initiatives from strategy through execution, without relying on the CEO to drive every decision.
 The role is channel agnostic. We don't care whether our next major growth opportunity comes from Meta advertising, Amazon external traffic, Shopify, TikTok Shop, creator partnerships, AI-powered content, or an entirely new channel. What matters is identifying where the greatest opportunities exist, validating them through disciplined experimentation, and allocating resources toward what produces profitable, incremental growth.
 Equally important is knowing what not to pursue. The Director of Ecommerce Growth must be willing to challenge existing strategies, stop underperforming initiatives, and redirect resources toward higher potential opportunities.
 The vision: Build a diversified, scalable, and profitable growth engine that consistently generates new customer demand, turns successful experiments into repeatable systems, and operates without requiring the CEO's daily involvement, ultimately helping Hadley Designs become a $100 million brand by 2030.
Metrics that You'll Own 
 Incremental Contribution Profit: Generate at least $1,000,000 in annual incremental contribution profit from growth initiatives, after all attributable variable marketing and program costs.
 Incremental Demand Generation Revenue : Generate at least $7,000,000 in annual incremental revenue through paid media, affiliate marketing, creator partnerships, and new acquisition channels, regardless of whether customers purchase through Amazon, Shopify, or TikTok Shop.
 Marketing Efficiency Ratio (MER): Achieve a minimum 3.0x blended MER across the defined growth portfolio, while meeting contribution profit targets. Final target subject to validated channel economics.
 Growth Experiments: Execute at least 1 meaningful growth experiments per month (12 annually), each with a documented hypothesis, an approved budget, contribution profit target, performance review, and predefined stop criteria.
 Scalable Growth Engines: From the list of 12 growth experiments, at least 3 new experiments are repeatable, profitable growth engines annually, each generating at least $25,000 in incremental monthly revenue with positive contribution profit for three consecutive months.
 Primary Objectives 20% BIG ROCKS – These must be done first and at all costs.
 Build a Repeatable, Profitable Demand Generation Engine: Develop and scale sustainable sources of customer acquisition and revenue across Amazon, Shopify, TikTok Shop, paid media, affiliates, and emerging channels, prioritizing incremental contribution profit over revenue alone.

Own execution plans, remove bottlenecks, and ensure growth initiatives deliver measurable results without requiring the CEO's daily involvement.

About the role: 
 Mercury is looking for a Model Risk Manager to help build and operate a practical, risk-based Model Risk Management program as we continue to scale and prepare for life as a regulated bank. 
 Models support an increasingly broad range of decisions across Mercury, including credit underwriting, portfolio management, fraud prevention, BSA/AML, CECL, finance, liquidity, pricing, and operational processes. This role will provide independent review and effective challenge throughout the model lifecycle while helping Mercury apply governance proportionate to the actual risk of each model.
 This is a hands-on role for someone who can move comfortably between technical analysis, regulatory expectations, and business context. You will conduct model validations, challenge assumptions and limitations, improve our model inventory and monitoring practices, and work closely with teams across Risk Ops, Data, Engineering, Product, Finance, Compliance, and Internal Audit. 
 Showing up as a true collaborator, advisor and partner to the business will be key as we continue to build out this function and work towards our collective goals at Mercury. You should be comfortable operating in a fast-moving environment where the objective is not governance for its own sake, but helping Mercury use models safely, responsibly, and effectively.
 What you’ll do: 
 Perform independent validations and reviews of internally developed and third-party models across areas such as credit, fraud, BSA/AML, CECL, finance, liquidity, pricing, and operational risk.
 Evaluate each model’s methodology, assumptions, data quality and lineage, implementation, and performance through reviews and testings such as outcomes analysis, benchmarking, back-testing, and sensitivity testing scaled to its risk and materiality.
 Provide credible and constructive challenges to model developers, owners, and users while maintaining effective working relationships with 1LOD.
 Assess model risk and materiality based on a model’s inherent risk, purpose, exposure, use, and potential impact.
 Help maintain a complete and accurate model inventory, including model ownership, risk rating, dependencies, limitations, validation status, monitoring requirements, and open issues.
 Review ongoing monitoring plans and results, including performance thresholds, overrides, data drift, model changes, and conditions that could make a model no longer fit for purpose.
 Evaluate vendor models and other third-party analytical products, including available documentation, transparency, performance, limitations, customization, and Mercury’s ability to monitor and control their use.
 Document validation conclusions clearly, identify issues, recommend proportionate remediation, and track findings through resolution.
 Support controlled model use when validation cannot be completed before implementation by helping establish appropriate limitations, compensating controls, monitoring, and approvals.
 Develop clear reporting on model risk, validation coverage, performance concerns, concentrations, dependencies, exceptions, and overdue remediation for management and governance committees.
 Help improve Mercury’s Model Risk Management Policy, standards, procedures, and templates.
 Use automation and analytical tools to make model inventory management, testing, monitoring, and reporting more efficient.
 Partner with Mercury’s Data and AI Governance teams to establish clear boundaries and handoffs between traditional model risk management and the governance of generative AI, agentic AI, and other analytical systems outside the formal model definition.
 Support regulatory examinations, Internal Audit reviews, and other assurance activities involving model risk.
 What we’re looking for: 
 5+ years of relevant experience in model validation, model development, quantitative risk analytics, or a related discipline within banking, fintech, financial services, or consulting.
 Bachelor’s degree in Statistics, Mathematics, Physics, Computer Science, Engineering, Financial Engineering or a related field. Master’s degree or PhD is preferred. 
 Strong knowledge of model risk management principles and current regulatory expectations, including the revised interagency guidance reflected in SR 26-2.
 Intensive experience validating or developing models in one or more areas such as BSA/AML, fraud, financial forecasting, CECL, capital, liquidity, and credit underwriting, using one or more methodologies such as machine learning (e.g., XGBoost, random forests), scorecards, complex vendor models (e.g., Alloy, Firco), and complex spreadsheet-based models.
 Proficiency with SQL and Python (from a data analytics lens); comfortable building understanding of models independently of their developers through collecting evidence and data analytics.
 Strong written and verbal communication skills; you can explain model risk to a data scientist and to a regulator, or translate your findings and recommendations to guidance for the 1LOD product/business teams, and use different language for each.
 Exceptional attention to detail across documentation, code base, testing artifacts and quantitative analysis provided by 1LOD.
 Sound judgment and a practical, risk-based mindset: you can distinguish significant model risk from lower-risk matters and have the confidence to challenge model owners constructively, including senior stakeholders.
 High ownership, intellectual curiosity, and comfort building processes in a fast evolving environment, where priorities evolve quickly, new ad hoc requests emerge regularly, and role boundaries are intentionally broad. You can operate effectively without tightly-defined scope, find the highest-leverage work, and get it done.
 Preferred qualifications: 
 Experience helping build or materially enhance a model risk management program.
 Familiarity with bank regulatory examinations, charter readiness, or the implementation of risk programs within a growing financial institution.
 Knowledge of Haskell
 What success looks like: 
 Mercury maintains a complete and reliable view of its material models and aggregate model risk.
 Critical models receive timely, technically credible, and risk-based independent review.
 Model limitations, performance concerns, and remediation needs are clearly understood and acted upon.
 Model owners view Model Risk as a rigorous and constructive partner that improves decisions without creating unnecessary friction.
 Mercury’s Model Risk Management program is scalable, practical, and ready to withstand regulatory and independent assurance review.
 *Mercury is a financial technology company, not a bank. Banking services provided through Choice Financial Group, Column N.A., and Evolve Bank & Trust, Members FDIC.

The total rewards package at Mercury includes base salary, equity (stock options/RSUs), and benefits.
 Our salary and equity ranges are highly competitive within the SaaS and fintech industry and are updated regularly using the most reliable compensation survey data for our industry. New hire offers are made based on a candidate’s experience, expertise, geographic location, and internal pay equity relative to peers.

 Participate in technical design discussions and architecture decisions for your area.

 Every feature our operators rely on — bookings, payments, waivers, reporting — is only as good as the engineering behind it. As we rebuild our product organization post-acquisition, the developers who join now will shape not just what gets built, but how reliably and how well it's built for years to come.
 You'll Thrive Here If... 
 You want ownership over how you solve a problem, not just a ticket to close.

 Introductory conversation

 Final decision
Join Us 
 We're building more than a codebase. We're building the engineering foundation that will define the next chapter of Clubspeed and Resova. If you're looking for a place where you'll be trusted with real ownership over your work, and rewarded for the outcomes you drive, we'd love to hear from you.

 3+ years of professional software development experience, ideally in SaaS or a high-growth product company.

La personne titulaire du poste est responsable d’anticiper les risques liés à la réalisation des projets, de coordonner les mesures correctives auprès des différentes parties prenantes, de diriger l’amélioration des processus et des systèmes et de favoriser l’exécution efficace de mandats clients à forte valeur ajoutée.  Réalisation et gouvernance des projets (50 %)

 The Specialist, Consulting Operations provides operational leadership for the delivery of consulting projects and operational excellence initiatives across Consulting Services. Working with Project Leads, technical leads, and senior leadership, this role drives project governance and operational planning, leads resource and capacity management processes, administers core business systems, and translates portfolio data into recommendations that inform delivery and business decisions.  travailler pour une entreprise reconnue dans des douzaines de pays partout dans le monde comme étant un excellent milieu de travail et figurant parmi les entreprises les plus admirées dans le monde dans le classement Fortune;

La mission de notre activité en cardiologie structurelle est de restaurer la santé et d’améliorer la qualité de vie grâce à la conception et à la fourniture de dispositifs et de solutions de gestion destinés au traitement des maladies cardiaques structurelles.

Cela se fait par la prestation de formation clinique et de soutien aux ventes afin de contribuer à l’atteinte des objectifs de ventes projetés et à l’augmentation des revenus générés par les gammes de produits assignées. The incumbent is responsible for securing, maintaining, and protecting the spectrum and orbital rights required to support Telesat's GSO and NGSO satellite systems. The role leads complex spectrum engineering, ITU filing and coordination activities; conducts interference and compatibility analyses; supports satellite system design from a spectrum and regulatory perspective; and represents Telesat in technical coordination discussions with satellite operators, administrations, and relevant domestic and international regulatory bodies. The position provides technical and regulatory advice that informs satellite system design, spectrum strategy, and regulatory decisions.

Main Responsibilities: Prepare, submit, and manage ITU satellite network and system filings and associated technical and regulatory showings in accordance with the ITU Radio Regulations, including applicable coordination and notification procedures.
 Collaborate with systems engineering, legal, business development, and other internal stakeholders to ensure satellite system designs and deployment plans are consistent with applicable spectrum and regulatory requirements and that associated filings accurately reflect system design and operational characteristics.
 Analyze ITU examination results and regulatory findings, determine appropriate technical and regulatory responses, and lead coordination activities with other satellite operators and administrations through to resolution.
 Perform interference, sharing, compatibility, and coordination analyses involving GSO and NGSO satellite networks and systems, other space services, and terrestrial services, including link-budget and carrier-level analyses as applicable.
 Prepare and manage domestic regulatory applications, filings, and associated technical submissions through to completion with relevant national authorities.
 Develop and support contributions to ITU-R Working Parties, relevant regional organizations and preparatory groups, and WRC processes in support of Telesat's spectrum and regulatory objectives.
 Prepare technical and regulatory analyses, coordination correspondence, briefing materials, recommendations, and presentations for internal stakeholders and senior management.
 Lead technical coordination discussions and negotiations with satellite operators and administrations and support the development and conclusion of coordination agreements.
 Provide strategic technical and regulatory advice and recommendations to senior management on spectrum access, protection, coordination, system design, and associated regulatory risks and opportunities.
Education & Experience: Bachelor's degree in Electrical, Telecommunications, Computer Engineering, or a related technical field; Master's degree preferred.
 Minimum 7 years of relevant professional experience in satellite spectrum engineering, RF engineering, satellite communications, or telecommunications regulatory engineering.
 Demonstrated experience applying the ITU Radio Regulations to satellite networks and systems, particularly Articles 9 and 11 and associated Rules of Procedure.
 Demonstrated proficiency in satellite link-budget, interference, compatibility, and coordination analysis.
 Experience with relevant ITU Radiocommunication Bureau software and databases used for satellite filing and coordination activities.
 Proficiency with analytical/programming tools such as Python or MATLAB; experience with commercial satellite-system or interference-analysis tools is an asset.
 Excellent written and oral communication skills in English, including the ability to communicate complex technical and regulatory matters to technical and non-technical audiences.
 Strong analytical, organizational, negotiation, and stakeholder-management skills.
Decision Making and Supervision: The incumbent exercises substantial independent technical judgment in the development and execution of spectrum filing, coordination, and interference-analysis strategies. The incumbent develops recommendations concerning the acquisition, maintenance, and protection of spectrum and orbital rights and advises on regulatory and spectrum-related constraints that may influence satellite system design and operations. Matters involving significant commercial, legal, policy, or corporate commitments are escalated to the appropriate decision-making authority.
 The role does not currently require direct people management but may provide technical leadership, mentoring, and guidance to engineers and other team members.
Working Conditions: Position is based in Ottawa, Ontario, with a hybrid work arrangement.
 Domestic and international travel may be required to support coordination negotiations, regulatory meetings, ITU-R activities, and related industry events.
